t: India's first legislation making third party motor insurance compulsory was the
e: The Motor Vehicles Act 1939, effective 01.07.1939, introduced compulsory TP insurance along with licensing and traffic regulation in India.

t: The 1988 Motor Vehicles Act was enacted on the recommendations of a committee of experts appointed in 1985 by
e: A GIC-appointed expert committee of 1985 led to the 1988 Act; the 1994 amendment added Sections 163A/163B on structured formula compensation.

t: Which of the following is one of the three categories of vehicles for motor insurance purposes?
e: The three classes are private cars, motorised two wheelers and commercial vehicles (GCCV, PCCV and miscellaneous).

t: Insurable interest in a motor vehicle may vest in all of the following EXCEPT
o: A regular passenger of the vehicle
e: Owner, dealer, hire purchase and hypothecation parties have insurable interest; a passenger has none in the vehicle itself.

t: The 1994 amendment to the MV Act (effective 14.11.1994) replaced medium and heavy goods/passenger vehicle categories with the single entry
e: The amendment merged MGV/MPV/HGV/HPV into 'Transport Vehicle' and replaced 'without gear' with 'up to 50 cc'.

t: A road roller driving licence is valid for
e: Road roller licences are valid for 3 years, minimum age 20, and require a medical certificate.

t: A licence for a geared motor cycle issued to a driver aged 52 is valid until
e: For a driver above 50 but below 55 at issue, validity runs till age 60; above 55 it is 5 years.

t: An owner must apply for registration within how many days of taking delivery of a vehicle?
e: The application for registration is to be made within 7 days of delivery; temporary registration is valid for one month.

t: Under Section 55, if a vehicle is found used in an offence under Section 199A, the RC may be cancelled for
e: After hearing the owner, the authority may cancel the RC for one year, after which fresh registration can be applied for.

t: Metal parts worth ₹40,000 are replaced on a car aged 3 years 8 months. The depreciation deducted on these parts is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). For a vehicle above 3 years but below 4 years, depreciation on metal parts is 25%, i.e. ₹10,000.

t: A certificate of fitness for a transport vehicle on renewal is valid for
e: Fitness is valid 2 years for a brand new transport vehicle and 1 year on each renewal, tested at an automated testing station.

t: A permit renewed after a gap of four months takes effect from
o: The date of expiry of the old permit
The first day of the following month
e: Renewal of a permit takes effect from the date of expiry even when there is a gap in renewal.

t: 'Golden hour' under Section 2(12A) refers to
o: The hour after sunrise when visibility is best
The hour within which police must be informed
The time within which an FIR must be lodged
One hour following a traumatic injury when prompt medical care is most likely to prevent death
e: The golden hour is the one hour after trauma with the highest chance of saving life; Section 162 provides for cashless treatment during it.

t: Under Section 129, the requirement to wear protective headgear on a motorcycle does not apply to
e: Every person above four years must wear a helmet, except a Sikh wearing a turban while driving or riding.

t: Under Section 110A, a manufacturer who detects a defect, informs the Central Government and initiates a voluntary recall
o: Must still pay the prescribed fine
Must replace all vehicles free of cost regardless
Loses the right to manufacture that model
Is not liable to pay fine
e: Voluntary disclosure and recall exempts the manufacturer from fine, though repair, replacement or refund obligations continue.

t: When the insured cancels the policy, premium is refunded
o: After retaining premium on short period scale
In full if no claim has arisen
e: Insured-initiated cancellation retains short period premium; insurer-initiated cancellation refunds pro-rata after 7 days notice.

t: The option to repair, replace or pay in cash after an accident rests with
o: The insurer, subject to the IDV
e: The policy gives the insurer the option to repair, reinstate or pay in cash, but the liability cannot exceed the IDV.

t: A car is damaged while being carried by rail. Under Section I this loss is
o: Covered only under a marine policy
Covered only if the railway admits liability
Covered, as transit by road, rail, inland waterway, lift, elevator or air is a listed peril
e: Transit by road, rail, inland waterway, lift, elevator or air is an insured peril under Section I.

t: OD premium on a private car is ₹6,000 and the insured is an Automobile Association member. The AA discount allowed is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR-28 allows 5% of OD premium (₹300) subject to a maximum of ₹200 for cars (₹50 for two wheelers).

t: For a private car used for driving tuition, the limitations as to use are modified by adding the words
o: 'other than for the purpose of driving tuition' after 'hire or reward'
e: The tariff directs insertion of 'other than for the purpose of driving tuition' after the words 'hire or reward' for tuition vehicles.

t: Under IMT-23, items excluded by IMT-21 can be covered on payment of extra premium, with the claim payable at
e: IMT-23 buys back the IMT-21 exclusion for commercial vehicles on extra premium, but only 50% of the loss is payable.

t: A fork lift truck used only within a factory can be insured for damage risks (other than road liability) under
o: A motor trade internal risks policy
e: For Class D vehicles such as fork lifts, cranes and excavators, cover other than road legal liability may be given under a non-motor policy.

t: GR-1 provides that motor insurance in India
o: Cannot be transacted outside the purview of the India Motor Tariff
May be transacted outside the tariff with IRDAI approval
Is governed by the Marine tariff for transit
e: GR-1 states that motor insurance in India cannot be transacted outside the purview of the India Motor Tariff.

t: A fresh proposal form is NOT required at renewal when the only change is
e: GR-2 requires a written proposal for new insurance and at renewal where there is material alteration, except a change in IDV.

t: The IDV depreciation for a vehicle aged above 4 years but not exceeding 5 years is
e: The IDV schedule reads 5%, 15%, 20%, 30%, 40% and 50% for the successive age bands up to 5 years.

t: Electrical fittings not included in the manufacturer's selling price are valued at ₹50,000. The additional OD premium under GR-41 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR-41 charges 4% on the value of such fittings, i.e. ₹2,000, provided they are specifically declared.

t: Partial loss depreciation on parts of a vehicle aged exactly 4 months is
e: For parts other than rubber/plastic/glass/fibre glass, depreciation is nil below 6 months, 5% for 6 months to 1 year, then 10%, 15%, 25%, 35%, 40% and 50%.

t: A tyre claim of ₹8,000 arises where the vehicle is also damaged in the accident. The amount admissible for the tyre (before deductible) is
e: Tyres attract 50% depreciation, so ₹4,000 is admissible when the vehicle is damaged at the same time.

t: A two wheeler registered at Hyderabad falls in which rating zone?
e: Hyderabad is among the eight Zone A cities for private cars and two wheelers.

t: For commercial vehicles other than those under 4.C.1 and 4.C.4, Zone A comprises
e: Commercial vehicle zoning: Zone A is the four metros, Zone B other State capitals, Zone C rest of India.

t: NCB is to be computed on the OD premium
o: After deducting the rebate for vehicle laid up
e: GR-27 directs NCB to be computed on OD premium after deducting the laid-up vehicle rebate.

t: An insured sells his car and does not replace it immediately. His NCB certificate remains valid for
o: 3 years from the expiry date of the previous insurance
e: GR-27: on sale without immediate replacement, NCB certificate is valid for 3 years from expiry of the previous insurance.

t: If Automobile Association membership is cancelled during the policy currency, the insurer should
o: Recover the discount on a pro-rata basis
e: GR-28: discount is allowed pro-rata for mid-term membership and recovered pro-rata if membership is cancelled mid-term.

t: Under GR-32, mid-term inclusion or cancellation of extra benefits in a policy is permitted
o: Not more than once during the policy currency
e: GR-32 prohibits mid-term inclusion/cancellation of extra benefits more than once during the currency of a policy.

t: Compulsory PA cover for owner-driver is available
o: Under both liability only and package policies
e: GR-36 CPA cover applies under both Liability Only and Package policies for the registered owner holding an effective licence.

t: A motorised two wheeler has an OD claim assessed at ₹3,600 after depreciation. The payable amount is
e: Compulsory deductible for two wheelers is ₹100, so ₹3,500 is payable.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

t: Under GR-40, compulsory deductibles apply also to
o: Restricted fire and/or theft covers under GR-45A/B
e: Compulsory deductibles apply to OD section claims for all vehicle classes and also where restricted fire/theft covers are granted.

t: Liability Only policy with fire-only cover is charged at liability premium plus
e: GR-45B: fire only 25%, theft only 30%, fire and theft 50% of the appropriate OD premium.

t: Restricted covers under GR-45A and GR-45B are prohibited for
o: Class D miscellaneous and special type vehicles
e: Both restricted covers are prohibited for Class D vehicles; GR-45A is additionally barred for Class E, F and G motor trade risks.

t: An insured opts for additional towing cover of ₹1,500 on his private car under GR-47. The extra premium is
e: GR-47 charges 5% of the amount opted; 5% of ₹1,500 is ₹75.

t: For an outstation survey involving overnight stay away from the normal place of work, the fee payable is
o: 100% of scale plus halting allowance only
150% of the amount determined as per the scale
e: Outstation spot/final/re-inspection surveys with overnight stay are paid at 150% of the scale fee.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

t: Where the repair estimate exceeds the IDV, the maximum survey fee is to be computed on
e: The schedule provides that if the estimate is more than the IDV, the maximum survey fee is based on IDV, not the estimate.

t: Under the 2024 master circular as summarised by the trainer, depreciation is NOT to be applied on
e: The circular directs that no depreciation be deducted on non-OEM/non-OES replacement parts.

t: Which add-on is generally offered only for the first 4 to 5 years of a vehicle?
e: NCB protection is generally available for the first 4-5 years and keeps the accrued NCB intact despite small OD claims.

t: Under a Motor Trade Road Risks policy, issuance of fire and/or theft cover without liability only cover is
e: Class F policies cannot be issued for fire and/or theft without the Liability Only cover.

t: Under Section 150(2), which of the following is NOT a defence available to the insurer?
o: Use for hire or reward without a permit
Driving by a person not duly licensed
Vehicle being driven above the speed limit
e: Statutory defences are limited to specified breaches (use, driver, war risks), policy void for non-disclosure and non-receipt of premium; speeding is not one.

t: Under Section 146, vehicles carrying dangerous or hazardous goods must additionally have
e: Section 146 makes a Public Liability Insurance policy mandatory for vehicles carrying dangerous or hazardous goods.

t: An application for compensation under Section 166 must be made within
e: The 2019 amendment restored a limitation of six months from the accident; a Section 159 police report is also treated as an application.
